summary: RAG best-of-4 with pairwise 3B tournament select
hypothesis: A pairwise 3B tournament over 4 RAG-drawn sets should outperform absolute scoring (exp004) and frequency clustering (exp010) because the 3B is better at relative than absolute judgment, letting it pick the coverage-richer set and lift quality above a single draw.
technique: Four independent RAG sets are drawn at temperatures [0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 0.9], then a single-elimination pairwise tournament uses the on-device 3B as judge — each match is run in both orderings (two-order vote, tie goes to lower-temp incumbent) to damp position bias; the tournament winner is returned verbatim.
result: Scored 0.297 on dev-10 (0 wins / 0 ties / 10 losses vs Sonnet), a step below the exp003 best (0.320), below exp011 (0.323), and even below the baseline (0.307). Coverage stayed at 3 and off-task questions persisted in the tournament winners, showing the 3B's pairwise verdict is not correlated with coverage of decision-critical unknowns — hypothesis falsified, discarded.
